question: Which of the activity deficits in the following enzymes of the urea cycle can cause an orotic aciduria, in addition to hyperammonemia ?:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency" -> "accumulation of carbamoyl phosphate" -> "excess carbamoyl phosphate enters pyrimidine synthesis" -> "increased orotic acid production" -> "orotic aciduria" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Arginase deficiency" -> "accumulation of arginine" -> "no direct link to orotic aciduria" -> "unclear mechanism for orotic aciduria" -> 20%
CHAIN: "Arginine succinate synthase deficiency" -> "accumulation of citrulline" -> "no direct link to orotic aciduria" -> "unclear mechanism for orotic aciduria" -> 20%
CHAIN: "Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase deficiency" -> "decreased carbamoyl phosphate" -> "reduced substrate for pyrimidine synthesis" -> "unlikely orotic aciduria" -> 10%
analysis: Ornithine transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency is a urea cycle disorder that can lead to the accumulation of carbamoyl phosphate. This excess carbamoyl phosphate is then converted into orotic acid, causing orotic aciduria. Additionally, OTC deficiency results in hyperammonemia due to the disruption of the urea cycle. Other enzyme deficiencies in the urea cycle, such as arginase, arginine succinate synthase, and carbamoyl phosphate synthetase, do not typically cause orotic aciduria.
